current_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens where the address returns to the masculine plural after the singular turn that closes at web:Isa.55.5: דִּרְשׁ֥וּ יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.55.6, byte tier), “Seek Yahweh while he may be found. Call on him while he is near.” (web:Isa.55.6) — the same plural-imperative form-class as the invitation cry's own opening imperatives, now turned to a summons-to-repentance address rather than a continuation of the come-buy-eat invitation of web:Isa.55.1-Isa.55.5. The ways/thoughts contrast follows at כִּ֣י לֹ֤א מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי֙ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם דְּרָכָ֑י נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.55.8, byte tier), “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways” (web:Isa.55.8), closing with the postpositive divine-speech signature that seals the exhortation's own reasoning. The row runs to the frame boundary at web:Isa.55.13|web:Isa.56.1, where the word's efficacy and the joy-departure close bring the exhortation to its resolution: “It will make a name for Yahweh, for an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.” (web:Isa.55.13). A setumah paragraph mark (single-witness, tier-3) closes at oshb:Isa.55.5, this row's own front-seam predecessor, and again at oshb:Isa.55.13, this row's own final verse.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative reads web:Isa.55.10-Isa.55.13 as a self-standing doxology closure rather than the consequence-clause of this row's own exhortation, since the nature-personification imagery there carries hymn-adjacent texture; this row instead keeps it inside the seek-Yahweh unit because no fresh imperative or addressee change opens web:Isa.55.10.
current_row.literature_type_guess: exhortation to seek Yahweh with closing assurance
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: This row's rear seam, at the frame boundary web:Isa.55.13|web:Isa.56.1, carries a byte-identical closing run on both sides: לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת (oshb:Isa.55.13, byte tier) and לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת (oshb:Isa.56.5, byte tier) are the same pointed form, standing at byte tier in exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses; its consonantal skeleton reaches three, adding oshb:Isa.48.19). The pairing argues continuity across the boundary, but the boundary itself is a preserved larger-unit seam that no internal device can move, so the disclosure stands without reopening it. A ketiv/qere pair sits at oshb:Isa.55.13 (byte tier, single-witness): the unpointed ketiv תחת runs immediately into the pointed qere with a prefixed conjunction, וְתַ֥חַת, in the source bytes, per the inventory rather than a retyped pair.

items.claim: The addressee-number driver yields two candidate seam positions and the row discloses neither the rival nor a discriminator: if the shift of addressee number is the warrant, the plural-to-singular turn at the front of oshb:Isa.55.5 is as much a seam as the singular-to-plural return at oshb:Isa.55.6, and the row's stated rival is a different one entirely.
items.proposed_change: Field repair only: disclose the cut-before-oshb:Isa.55.5 rival as the strongest one and name the byte-grounded discriminator that keeps the singular verse with the invitation rather than with the summons.
items.adjudicator_grounds: The bytes re-derive as filed: a plural addressee through oshb:Isa.55.3 (אָזְנְכֶם֙ and נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם, oshb:Isa.55.3, byte tier), no second person in oshb:Isa.55.4, a wholly masculine-singular oshb:Isa.55.5 (from תֵדַע֙ to פֵאֲרָֽךְ, oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier), and a return to plural imperatives at דִּרְשׁ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.55.6, byte tier); הַטּ֤וּ (oshb:Isa.55.3, byte tier) is likewise verse-initial inside the preceding span. The single-witness inventory carries SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.55.5 and nothing at oshb:Isa.55.4 - tier-3, never a discriminator. The row's boundary_rationale never mentions a cut before oshb:Isa.55.5, and its strongest_rejected_alternative addresses a rear rival (web:Isa.55.10-Isa.55.13 as a doxology closure) - not, as the finding's grounds say, an undivided-chapter reading, which is the preceding row's rival; the claim that the nearer rival is undisclosed stands either way. The finding overstates one point: a byte discriminator does exist - oshb:Isa.55.6 opens on the imperative דִּרְשׁ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.55.6, byte tier), whereas oshb:Isa.55.5 opens on the presentative הֵ֣ן (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier), which matches הֵ֛ן opening oshb:Isa.55.4 (oshb:Isa.55.4, byte tier) at accent_stripped tier, a paired presentative onset binding the singular verse to the Davidic-witness verse before it; so of the two turn positions only the cut before oshb:Isa.55.6 carries an imperative onset. The row names that imperative form-class but never deploys it against the nearer rival, which is live (a verse-boundary cut on the row's own addressee-number driver class, unlike a mid-sentence switch), so the front-seam warrant is defective, not merely under-disclosed: medium confirmed. The proposed field repair is right; no span change.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The vocative onset וְאַתֶּ֥ם קִרְבוּ הֵ֖נָּה בְּנֵ֣י עֹנְנָ֑ה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.57.3, byte tier) -- “But draw near here, you sons of a sorceress, you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes.” (web:Isa.57.3) -- opens the address in second-person masculine plural, continued by עַל מִי֙ תִּתְעַנָּ֔גוּ (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.57.4) and its own plural pronoun. No finite second-person form appears at web:Isa.57.5, a participial chain describing the ritual acts rather than addressing anyone directly. From שָׁפַ֥כְתְּ נֶ֨סֶךְ֙ הֶעֱלִ֣ית מִנְחָ֔ה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.57.6) onward, every second-person form in the span is feminine singular, continuing unbroken to the row's own close: “but he who takes refuge in me will possess the land, and will inherit my holy mountain.” (web:Isa.57.13), spliced at the feminine suffixes of בְּזַֽעֲקֵךְ֙ יַצִּילֻ֣ךְ קִבּוּצַ֔יִךְ (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.57.13). The row holds this grammatical turn -- masculine plural giving way to feminine singular at the MT 57:4 | MT 57:6 junction -- as its own live uncertainty rather than a break, since no vocative or frame marker of the tier-1 class accompanies the shift; the row closes at web:Isa.57.13, the verse just before the third-person messenger introduction “He will say” that opens a fresh unit at web:Isa.57.14.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading cuts a fresh row at the grammatical turn from second-person masculine plural to second-person feminine singular, splitting web:Isa.57.3-Isa.57.5 from web:Isa.57.6-Isa.57.13 at that junction; the row holds the whole span as one continuous idolatry indictment instead, since no vocative or frame marker of the tier-1 class accompanies the grammatical shift.
current_row.literature_type_guess: judgment oracle against idolatrous ritual practice, addressed first to the sons of the sorceress in the plural and then to the personified unfaithful city in the feminine singular

current_row.device_notes: No petuchah/setumah break falls at this row's own front seam, within its span, or on its closing verse in the marks inventory; the row's silence on the mark layer here is itself the span-relevant absence. The lofty-epithet form closing this row's own front descriptor, וְנִשָּׂ֔א (oshb:Isa.57.7), and the form opening the divine epithet just past this row's own closing seam, וְנִשָּׂ֗א (oshb:Isa.57.15), are not byte-identical -- they differ in accentuation -- and collate at accent-stripped tier only, where the form stands in 6 verses book-wide; the pair straddles this row's own rear seam and is disclosed here without moving it.

items.claim: The row's rear-seam driver is a Hebrew form-class claim about MT 57:14 that is carried on the English witness alone: no pointed splice and no oshb:Isa.57.14 entry in boundary_evidence_refs.
items.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): splice וְאָמַ֥ר (oshb:Isa.57.14, byte tier) into boundary_rationale beside the existing WEB citation and add oshb:Isa.57.14 to boundary_evidence_refs.
items.adjudicator_grounds: MT 57:14 opens verse-initially on וְאָמַ֥ר (oshb:Isa.57.14, byte tier), the waw-plus-perfect third-person-singular speech-introduction verb that both witnesses carry as 'He will say' (web:Isa.57.14); the verse continues סֹֽלּוּ סֹ֖לּוּ פַּנּוּ דָ֑רֶךְ (oshb:Isa.57.14, byte tier), so the row's rear-seam claim is byte-true. The shipped row's boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.57.14 but no oshb:Isa.57.14 while pairing oshb refs for 57:3, 57:4, 57:6, 57:7, 57:13 and 57:15, and boundary_rationale quotes no Hebrew for the seam driver; the book-order neighbor row opening at 57:14 splices the same form at byte tier. The mark inventory keys no seg at MT 57:13 (the next keyed seg is the SAMEKH at 57:14), so the seam has no tier-3 corroboration and rests on this verb-form onset alone. The engagement-class law makes a pointed splice plus tier label mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim; a load-bearing seam driver carried on the English witness alone is a defective warrant, not a mechanical shortfall, and the byte-truth of the claim keeps the boundary itself sound, so nothing rises to high. Medium as filed. The proposed field repair (splice the form beside the WEB citation and add oshb:Isa.57.14) stands, with no seam movement.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens on a voice shift argued from the verb bytes themselves: עַל כֵּ֗ן רָחַ֤ק מִשְׁפָּט֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.9, byte tier) -- “Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness doesn’t overtake us.” (web:Isa.59.9) -- reaches its first true first-person-plural verbs later in the same verse, נְקַוֶּ֤ה and נְהַלֵּֽךְ (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.9), “We look for light ... we walk in obscurity.” -- a form-class claim argued from the pointed bytes themselves plus both witnesses' renderings, since no morphology layer is staged for independent verification. The confession continues in first-person-plural verb forms through web:Isa.59.9-Isa.59.14: כָּשַׁ֤לְנוּ (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.10), “We stumble at noon as if it were twilight.” (web:Isa.59.10), “We all roar like bears” (web:Isa.59.11), and וַעֲוֺנֹתֵ֖ינוּ יְדַֽעֲנֽוּם (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.12), “our transgressions are multiplied before you ... we know them” (web:Isa.59.12), none of them narrative wayyiqtol forms. The row closes on “Justice is turned away backward, and righteousness stands far away; for truth has fallen in the street, and uprightness can’t enter.” (web:Isa.59.14), the verse just before the wayyiqtol chain that opens the divine-warrior narrative at web:Isa.59.15 -- the row's own closing argument rests on that verb-form shift rather than on the topical content of web:Isa.59.15 alone, since the verse's own first clause is grammatically part of the narrative chain that follows it, not the confession that precedes it.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading attaches the first clause of web:Isa.59.15 ('truth is lacking') to this row as the confession's own summary line, cutting the row at Isa.59.15 rather than Isa.59.14, since its content still catalogues the community's failure of justice.
current_row.literature_type_guess: communal confession cataloguing societal injustice in first-person-plural voice

current_row.device_notes: The oss tag here names the nearest taxonomy class for what is, precisely, a grammatical PERSON/voice shift (third-person description to first-person-plural confession) rather than a change of addressee; no petuchah/setumah break falls at this row's own front seam or within its span in the marks inventory. The no-justice phrase closing the verse just before this row's own front seam, וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט (oshb:Isa.59.8), and the phrase closing the verse just after this row's own rear seam, אֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּֽט (oshb:Isa.59.15), share their unprefixed core at skeleton tier (sweep: 2 verses book-wide) and bracket the row's whole span without falling inside it; the broader justice noun that both draw on stands in 40 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, 5 of them in this chapter (Isa.59.8, 59.9, 59.11, 59.14, 59.15). Neither the bracket nor the chapter's density of the term moves either of this row's own seams.

items.claim: The row's span-cohesion warrant — that first-person-plural verb forms continue through web:Isa.59.9-Isa.59.14 — overreaches its own bytes by two verses.
items.proposed_change: Field repair: restrict the first-person-plural form claim to web:Isa.59.9-Isa.59.12 and argue 59:13-59:14 on their own ground (the infinitive-absolute catalogue of the confession's own transgressions at MT 59:13 and the third-person summary at MT 59:14 standing before the wayyiqtol onset).
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived token by token at byte tier, with no morphology layer staged, so form classes are read from the pointed bytes and both witnesses' renderings as the campaign requires. First-person-plural finite verbs stand at נְקַוֶּ֤ה and נְהַלֵּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.59.9), נְגַֽשְׁשָׁ֤ה, נְגַשֵּׁ֑שָׁה, כָּשַׁ֤לְנוּ (oshb:Isa.59.10), נֶהֱמֶ֤ה, נֶהְגֶּ֑ה, נְקַוֶּ֤ה (oshb:Isa.59.11), and last at יְדַֽעֲנֽוּם (oshb:Isa.59.12), 'we know them' (web:Isa.59.12). MT 59:13 carries no finite first-person form: פָּשֹׁ֤עַ וְכַחֵשׁ֙, וְנָס֖וֹג, דַּבֶּר and הֹר֧וֹ וְהֹג֛וֹ (oshb:Isa.59.13, byte tier) are infinitive-absolute forms, rendered participially as 'transgressing and denying Yahweh, and turning away ... speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering' (web:Isa.59.13), and the verse's only first-person element is the plural suffix on אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ (oshb:Isa.59.13, byte tier). MT 59:14, וְהֻסַּ֤ג אָחוֹר֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה מֵרָח֣וֹק תַּעֲמֹ֑ד כִּֽי כָשְׁלָ֤ה בָֽרְחוֹב֙ אֱמֶ֔ת וּנְכֹחָ֖ה לֹא תוּכַ֥ל לָבֽוֹא (oshb:Isa.59.14, byte tier), carries no first-person form of any kind: וְהֻסַּ֤ג (oshb:Isa.59.14, byte tier) is a passive third-person waw-perfect and תַּעֲמֹ֑ד, כָשְׁלָ֤ה and תוּכַ֥ל (oshb:Isa.59.14, byte tier) are third-person feminine forms, matching 'Justice is turned away backward ... uprightness can't enter.' (web:Isa.59.14). The row's sentence that the confession 'continues in first-person-plural verb forms through web:Isa.59.9-Isa.59.14' is therefore byte-false for its last two verses, exactly as filed, while the row's own splices stop at 59:12. The defect is not load-bearing: the front seam rests on the person shift at עַל כֵּ֗ן רָחַ֤ק מִשְׁפָּט֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ (oshb:Isa.59.9, byte tier) and the rear seam on the wayyiqtol onset וַתְּהִ֤י הָֽאֱמֶת֙ נֶעְדֶּ֔רֶת (oshb:Isa.59.15, byte tier), both of which re-derive. MT 59:13 continues the confession as the object catalogue of 59:12's 'we know them', which is the ground the repair should state for it. Medium as filed; the proposed restriction of the form claim to 59:9-59:12 with separate grounds for 59:13-59:14 stands.

items.claim: The device_notes bracket mis-states where the no-justice phrase stands in MT 59:8: it is mid-verse, not verse-closing.
items.proposed_change: Field repair: state the MT 59:8 occurrence as mid-verse (before that verse's own caesura) rather than verse-closing, keeping the two digits as swept.
items.adjudicator_grounds: MT 59:8 is sixteen tokens: דֶּ֤רֶךְ שָׁלוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתָ֑ם נְתִיבֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ עִקְּשׁ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם כֹּ֚ל דֹּרֵ֣ךְ בָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א יָדַ֖ע שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier). The phrase וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט stands as tokens five and six, immediately before the athnach-bearing בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתָ֑ם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier), and the verse closes on לֹ֥א יָדַ֖ע שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier); the finding's own position digit is off by one (it says fourth and fifth), but its claim is byte-true: the phrase is mid-verse before the caesura, not verse-closing. The device_notes sentence applies 'closing the verse' to both members of its bracket, and that is true only of the partner: אֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּֽט (oshb:Isa.59.15, byte tier) is tokens twelve and thirteen of thirteen, verse-final. The digits re-derive at skeleton tier: אין משפט (skeleton tier) in 2 verses book-wide, 59:8 and 59:15, 2 tokens; the justice noun משפט (skeleton tier, substring sweep) in 40 verses book-wide, 42 tokens, 5 verses in this chapter (59:8, 59:9, 59:11, 59:14, 59:15). The mis-stated position is a byte-false claim inside a texture disclosure that the row itself says moves neither seam, so it is not load-bearing. Medium as filed; the proposed correction to mid-verse before that verse's own caesura, digits kept as swept, stands.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A first-person speaker announces a commission, “The Lord Yahweh's Spirit is on me, because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble.” (web:Isa.61.1), matching ר֛וּחַ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה עָלָ֑י (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier). A chain of purpose infinitives governed by that same sending — to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty and release, to comfort mourners, to give a garland for ashes — runs to the verse's own caesura at כֵּהָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) and continues, not as a further infinitive but as a waw-plus-perfect finite clause naming the mourners themselves as its subject, וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier): “that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.” (web:Isa.61.3), matching מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier). Isa.61.4 opens a further waw-plus-perfect clause with a changed subject, “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4) — the third-person-plural community now rebuilding, distinct from the mourners just named and called a planting at the unit's own close — marking this unit's close.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the first-person mission statement as continuing through Isa.61.4's building report was rejected because the infinitive-purpose chain governed by Yahweh's sending closes at Isa.61.3's own glorification clause, and Isa.61.4 opens a new finite-verb clause with a third-person-plural subject. Labeling the unit servant_song was considered and set aside because this unit's own bytes lack the eved-root vocabulary that anchors the book's servant census, leaving the anointed speaker's identity an open question the unit does not resolve.
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: A setumah (single-witness) at oshb:Isa.60.22 closes the preceding unit immediately before this one opens; a paseq (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position asserted) sits at oshb:Isa.61.3, inside this unit's own span. The catchword closing this unit is tier-mixed, not uniformly byte-true: the 'to be glorified' verb is byte-identical between the two units, לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier) and לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), but the paired planting noun is not — oshb:Isa.60.21 stages the ketiv/qere pair מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י (unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere) against this unit's own מַטַּ֥ע (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), the two meeting only at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses book-wide on that consonantal string). This tier-mixed catchword is disclosed here rather than treated as evidence against the boundary already argued from the subject shift at Isa.61.4. Labeling this unit servant_song was weighed and set aside: this unit's own bytes (Isa.61.1-Isa.61.3) lack the eved-root servant vocabulary that anchors the book's own servant census, so the identity of the anointed first-person speaker stays an open question this unit does not resolve.

items.claim: The rear seam at 61:3 | 61:4 rests on a 'changed subject' that MT 61:4 never states, and the row's own wording concedes the construction runs on across the seam.
items.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): re-argue the rear seam from the first-person commissioned-speaker frame that ends at 61:3 against the subjectless third-person report opening at MT 61:4, drop the unstated-referent claim, and re-cut rejected_alternative on the replacement warrant — noting that observed_substrate_signals, unit_type and confidence are dependent fields of any driver swap.
items.adjudicator_grounds: MT 61:4 reads וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם שֹׁמְמ֥וֹת רִֽאשֹׁנִ֖ים יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ עָ֣רֵי חֹ֔רֶב שֹׁמְמ֖וֹת דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier): three third-person-plural verbs, וּבָנוּ֙, יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ and וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), with no nominal subject anywhere in the verse, and the nearest plural antecedent is the dative party of וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), the mourners renamed 'trees of righteousness' (web:Isa.61.3); 'They will rebuild the old ruins.' (web:Isa.61.4) names no other referent in either witness. So the row's 'changed subject ... distinct from the mourners just named' is not stated by the bytes and runs against the nearest antecedent chain, as filed. The row's construction-class warrant is non-discriminating by its own wording: וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) is a waw-plus-perfect finite clause and וּבָנוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) another, which the row itself calls 'a further waw-plus-perfect clause'; the row also labels the mourners that clause's subject when the bytes make them its dative. The seam is not thereby shown wrong: the purpose-infinitive chain governed by שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier) does end at 61:3, since 61:4 opens on a finite form and not an infinitive, and the commissioned speaker's first-person forms עָלָ֑י, אֹתִ֜י and שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier) have no counterpart in 61:4-61:9, where the only first-person elements are the plural suffix on אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier) and the divine self-declaration אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.61.8, byte tier), objects the replacement warrant must name as distinct from the speaker's voice. The mark inventory keys no seg at MT 61:4; the paseq at 61:3 is count-only. A defective warrant beside a surviving byte-true ground, not alone load-bearing: medium as filed. The proposed re-argument from the first-person commission frame, with observed_substrate_signals, unit_type, rejected_alternative and confidence treated as dependent fields, stands as a field repair with no seam movement.

readjudication.grounds: Filed ground re-derived from bytes: the row's whole front-seam driver quotes וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), matching “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4), and its boundary_evidence_refs carry neither oshb:Isa.61.3 nor web:Isa.61.3; MT 61:3 closes on וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), matching “that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.” (web:Isa.61.3), so the finite waw-plus-perfect third-person construction the row names stands on both sides of the seam and discriminates nothing, exactly as filed. The finding's remaining ground ('no vocative, imperative onset, messenger frame, wayyiqtol onset or addressee change stands at MT 61:4') was onset-only, so per the re-adjudication instruction the seam was re-ruled on the complete both-sides test. Side (a), the row's own first verse: וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם שֹׁמְמ֥וֹת רִֽאשֹׁנִ֖ים יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ עָ֣רֵי חֹ֔רֶב שֹׁמְמ֖וֹת דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) carries no vocative, no imperative, no divine-speech, massa or hoy frame (the device inventory's koh-amar 48-verse, neum 23-verse, amar-YHWH-adjacency 52-verse, massa and hoy censuses key 0 sites in MT ch 61), and no addressee shift, the unit's second-person-plural address first appearing at צֹאנְכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.61.5, byte tier) and וְאַתֶּ֗ם כֹּהֲנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ תִּקָּרֵ֔אוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier): no ruled tier-1 onset. Side (b), the preceding unit's last verse, weighed under the refrain-close rule: 61:3's closing word לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) byte-recurs at exactly one other site, לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses book-wide on the pointed form), where it closes a verse inside the preceding unit rather than that unit's close, which falls at 60:22 on the divine self-identification אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.60.22, byte tier); and its paired planting noun is not byte-shared, the 60:21 ketiv/qere pair נֵ֧צֶר מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier; a K/Q verse in the inventory, checked before slicing) meeting 61:3's מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) only at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses on that consonantal string, 14:19 included). One non-terminal recurrence with a tier-mixed partner shows no bracket function, so 'refrains close units' does not warrant 61:3 as a close, and no closing formula stands there (neum and amar-YHWH censuses: 0 sites in MT ch 61). Result of the complete test: no ruled tier-1 signal on either side of 61:3|61:4. The seam's only available warrant is the frame-scope close the finding's repair names, and the bytes support it at verse granularity with a qualification the repair must carry: the first-person commission opens at ר֛וּחַ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה עָלָ֑י (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier) with אֹתִ֜י and שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier); its purpose-infinitive chain runs through לָשׂ֣וּם and לָתֵת֩ לָהֶ֨ם (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier); the turn to the waw-plus-perfect result chain happens inside 61:3 at וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier); and וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) continues that chain with an unexpressed third-person-plural subject whose nearest antecedent is 61:3's own plural pronoun (whole-token consonantal count of that pronoun in MT 61:1-9: 4 tokens, 61:3 twice, 61:7 לָהֶֽם and 61:8 אֶכְר֥וֹת לָהֶֽם, byte tier, none in 61:1-2). So 61:3|61:4 is the first verse boundary after the frame's governed chain is exhausted, and no clause spans it: 61:3 ends a complete clause closed by its own purpose infinitive, so the one-sentence rule (a syntactically continuous sentence spanning verses is one unit) does not bind, and 61:4 opens a new clause with its own object. The replacement warrant therefore passes the discrimination test that killed the original only when stated as a frame-scope close, never as a construction contrast, and it must disclose the cross-seam continuity it survives: the waw-plus-perfect chain and the plural referent run across the seam; the first-person-plural לֵאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ (oshb:Isa.61.2, byte tier) recurs as אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier; sweep: 14 verses book-wide on the consonantal string, these two the only chapter-61 sites), placing the speaker's self-inclusive voice on both sides; and the first person at כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.61.8, byte tier; וְנָתַתִּ֤י, אֶכְר֥וֹת לָהֶֽם) is YHWH's own voice, a distinct object from the anointed speaker's (the self-identification's consonantal string: sweep 22 verses, 60:22 and 61:8 included; the 61:8 pointed form byte-recurs in 9 verses). Tier-3, single witness: SAMEKH keyed at 60:22 and 61:9, a count-only paseq at 61:3, no seg at 61:4; absence is never counterevidence and nothing in that layer drives this ruling; the sentence break the translation prints before “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4) is translation punctuation and drives nothing. Prior adjudication: it confirmed medium on the frame-scope ground without running the refrain-close test on 61:3; the complete test returns the same outcome, so the verdict is unchanged, but its 'nothing in 61:4-61:9 resumes that voice' needs the qualifications above (the shared plural referent and the first-person-plural form on both sides). Governing rule: a front seam is warranted by a ruled tier-1 onset in the row's first verse or a ruled tier-1 close, refrain-close under the strategy, in the preceding unit's last verse; neither is present, and the seam survives on a frame-scope close the row never states: a warrant defect, not a disclosure gap (low) and not an unwarranted seam (high), because the frame-scope close is byte-supportable at verse granularity and the row's rear seam at 61:10, שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier, a new first-person voice), is untouched. Confirm at the filed medium; the field repair stands with no seam movement: state the frame-scope close against MT 61:3's bytes, add oshb:Isa.61.3 and web:Isa.61.3 to boundary_evidence_refs, re-cut rejected_alternative to the rival the bytes actually pose (61:4-61:9 read as the continuation of the commission speech of 61:1-61:3, grounded in the shared waw-plus-perfect chain and plural referent), and treat observed_substrate_signals and confidence as dependent fields. Coherence with the preceding row's side of the same seam: its 'changed subject' reason is not byte-discriminating either, since 61:4 names no new subject, so the pair's shared seam rests on the one frame-scope close and both rows' repairs are one edit.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. Plural address is already live before the seam: הַמַּזְכִּרִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) identifies the addressees by a participle, and אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) plus וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.7, byte tier) are second-person-masculine-plural (2mp) forms. MT 62:10 then carries six 2mp imperatives with no addressee named anywhere in the verse: עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), פַּנּ֖וּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), סֹ֣לּוּ סֹ֤לּוּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), סַקְּל֣וּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier) and הָרִ֥ימוּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier). The bytes thus establish a content turn (from the charge to give Yahweh no rest to gate, highway and banner commands) under an unbroken 2mp address; they cannot establish that the 62:10 group differs from the 62:6-7 group, which is what the row's ground 'addressed to an unnamed group rather than continuing the charge just laid on the watchmen' asserts. The book-order neighbor row argues the identical seam as 'not a shift to an unnamed addressee but a shift in content' and repeats the rejection in its rejected alternative, so the two rows carry incompatible warrants for one seam, and the neighbor's framing is the one the bytes support. One overstatement in the finding is noted without effect on the verdict: at 62:6 the plural addressees are identified by הַמַּזְכִּרִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) whereas at 62:10 they are not, so the group is in fact more unnamed at 62:10; that is a naming fact, not an addressee change, and the row's warrant still asserts a discontinuity the bytes cannot carry. The seam survives on the doubled verse-initial imperative and the content turn, with a SAMEKH at MT 62:9 in the paragraph-mark inventory (single witness, tier 3), so this is a defective warrant, not a boundary defect: medium as filed.

items.claim: The rear-seam driver — a Hebrew form-class claim about MT 62:10 — is carried on the English witness alone.
items.proposed_change: Field repair: splice עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier) beside the WEB citation and add oshb:Isa.62.10 to boundary_evidence_refs.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from the shipped row and the bytes. The row's rear-seam sentence carries the Hebrew form-class claim 'a fresh plural-imperative summons' with only the English witness “Go through, go through the gates!” (web:Isa.62.10), which does not mark number; its boundary_evidence_refs pair an oshb entry with every other web verse they cite (62:6, 62:7, 62:8, 62:9 as a setumah entry) but carry no oshb:Isa.62.10, and no Hebrew from that verse appears in any field of the row. The claim itself is byte-true: עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier) opens the verse with a doubled 2mp imperative, and the book-order neighbor row splices exactly this run at byte tier for the same seam. Under the engagement-class rule a form-class label on a seam driver is a byte-checkable claim carrying the same discipline as a digit and requiring a pointed splice with its tier named, so a rear-seam driver carried on the English witness alone is an unsupported warrant as shipped rather than a mechanical omission; it is not load-bearing beyond repair because the claim re-derives true and the seam is independently secured by the neighbor row's splice and the SAMEKH at MT 62:9 (single witness, tier 3): medium as filed.

current_row.boundary_rationale: This unit is bounded by a dramatic question-and-answer frame: the prophetic voice opens with a verse-initial interrogative, מִי זֶ֣ה בָּ֣א מֵאֱד֗וֹם (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier), “Who is this who comes from Edom” (web:Isa.63.1); the clause that follows opens instead on a bare demonstrative, זֶ֚ה הָד֣וּר בִּלְבוּשׁ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier), rendered as a second question, “Who is this who is glorious in his clothing,” only in the English witness. The challenged figure answers in the first person, closing that reply with "אֲנִ֛י מְדַבֵּ֥ר בִּצְדָקָ֖ה רַ֥ב לְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ" (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier) ('I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save'). A further verse-initial interrogative opens the next verse, מַדּ֥וּעַ (oshb:Isa.63.2, byte tier), “Why is your clothing red” (web:Isa.63.2), continuing the exchange. The same first-person divine-warrior voice continues in unbroken speech through the vengeance-and-treading report, closing the unit at “I poured their lifeblood out on the earth.” (web:Isa.63.6). The unit ends there because 63:7 pivots to a different speaker and a different speech-act: a first-person-plural recital of Yahweh's mercies replaces the divine warrior's own first-person report, with no further interrogative sustaining the dialogue frame.

current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the exchange into a two-verse question (63:1-2) and a four-verse answer (63:3-6) was considered and rejected because the whole exchange reads as one uninterrupted speech event between a single pair of voices — a challenger who twice opens with an interrogative, at Isa.63.1 and again at Isa.63.2, and a warrior who answers throughout — rather than as two separate dialogues.
current_row.literature_type_guess: divine-warrior victory report in dialogue form
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: The unit is a dramatic dialogue rather than a plain announcement -- a questioner voice and an answering warrior voice, a form closer to the ch. 21 watchman scene than to a standard judgment announcement -- disclosed as a deviation within the judgment_oracle operative category since the closed vocabulary has no dedicated dialogue value. The paragraph-mark inventory records a SAMEKH break at the verse immediately before this unit (Isa.62.12) and another SAMEKH break at its own close (Isa.63.6) -- tier-3 corroboration, single-witness, not a boundary driver.

items.claim: The rear-seam warrant is byte-false: MT 63:7 does not open a first-person-plural recital, and no change of grammatical person occurs across the seam.
items.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement; the seam itself survives on the speech-act change and the tier-3 SAMEKH already disclosed at MT 63:6): delete the 'first-person-plural recital' ground, re-argue the seam as a change of speech-act at unchanged grammatical person, splice חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), add oshb:Isa.63.7 to boundary_evidence_refs, and re-test confidence and frontier_flag now that the person-shift ground is withdrawn.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. MT 63:6 closes in the first-person singular (1cs): וְאָב֤וּס עַמִּים֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier) and וְאוֹרִ֥יד (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier) are 1cs verbs with a 1cs suffix. MT 63:7 opens חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier) with a first-person SINGULAR hiphil imperfect, rendered “I will tell of the loving kindnesses of Yahweh” (web:Isa.63.7); the verse's only first-person-plural element is the object suffix in גְּמָלָ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), and it contains no first-person-plural verb, so the row's 'a first-person-plural recital of Yahweh's mercies replaces the divine warrior's own first-person report' is byte-false as a person contrast: grammatical person is unchanged across the seam, exactly as the book-order neighbor row states. The row also cites web:Isa.63.7 with no oshb:Isa.63.7 entry and no splice from the verse its rear seam turns on, and ships at confidence high with frontier_flag_considered false. The finding is confirmed as to fact; the filed severity is not. Tested the other way, against the row's own seam: the divine name stands in the third person three times under that 1cs verb, in חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), תְּהִלֹּ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier) and גְּמָלָ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), which by itself separates the 63:7 speaker from the warrior who at וְאָב֤וּס עַמִּים֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier) reports his own deeds; the speech-act change (recital versus action report) is byte-grounded at the same verb; MT 63:7 carries no interrogative, so the row's 'no further interrogative sustaining the dialogue frame' is byte-true; and the paragraph-mark inventory records a SAMEKH at MT 63:6 (single witness, tier 3; MT 63:7 holds only a count-layer paseq seg). The seam therefore survives with the person-shift descriptor deleted, which the finding's own proposed change concedes ('the seam itself survives on the speech-act change and the tier-3 SAMEKH'). Under the severity law a byte-false claim is high only where it is load-bearing; this descriptor is one of four grounds in the rear-seam sentence and the boundary at 63:6|63:7 does not depend on it, so it is a defective warrant claim not alone load-bearing: downgraded to medium, with the missing oshb:Isa.63.7 engagement and the unrevisited high confidence noted as aggravating but not boundary-affecting.
